chunks: Aaban narrated from Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out of his chamber, and Marwan and his father were listening to his narration. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: “The lizard, son of a lizard!” Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: “From that day, they report that the lizard listens to the narration.”'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet calling Marwan 'the lizard, son of a lizard'?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) recounts how the Prophet Muhammad (saww) called Marwan ibn al-Hakam 'the lizard, son of the lizard' while Marwan and his father were eavesdroing on his private conversation. This incident highlights the Prophet's acute awareness of the eavesdroppers and serves as a basis for the belief that the lizard itself was listening, reflecting the Shia understanding of the Prophet's spiritual insight (basirah) and the connection between the physical and spiritual realms.
